evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

step_1_row_count_is_six.claim: The Syndra rotation at splinters = 120 has exactly six slot rows, so exactly six dependency ledgers.
derivation: data/champions.json Syndra exposes five wiki ability slots: P Transcendent, Q Dark Sphere, W Force of Will, E Scatter the Weak, R Unleashed Power.

Q's Transcendent Bonus (wiki, quoted below) adds a SECOND Dark Sphere charge once 40 Splinters are collected. The scenario name pins splinters = 120, and 120 >= 40, so the second-charge row is live and is a distinct rotation row.
data/champion-audit/batch-6.json independently records the modeled slot set as exactly [P, Q, Q2, W, E, R] - six - and names Q2 as 'synthetic Q2 (2nd charge)'.
Therefore six rows carry ledgers. (Counter-check: at splinters < 40 the count would be five, so six is specific to this scenario's 120 setting, not a constant.)

step_2_two_rows_are_unconsulted.claim: Exactly two rows must be recorded as `unconsulted` rather than as ledgers.
derivation: data/champion-audit/batch-6.json lists exactly two out_of_scope entries for Syndra: (a) 'E/W CC (stun, knockback, slow - utility only)' and (b) 'R 100-splinter execute (documented not modeled)'.

Both are non-damage / not-modeled rows. A resolver has nothing to resolve for a row the engine does not price, so the honest record is `unconsulted` - not an empty ledger, which would falsely assert 'consulted, found nothing'.

step_3_the_six_ledgers_are_correctly_emp.claim: Every one of the six ledgers should be empty for this scenario.
derivation: Ordering source: docs/math-foundations.md Sec. 1.1 states the engine's own ordering rule - 'the shared-timeline version is the superposition with mutual-exclusion, resolved greedily by cast order'. This scenario is a CUSTOM order supplied by a hand seed, so the ordering decision is exogenous; the resolver has no edge to derive. Empty ledgers are the faithful record of 'consulted, zero edges'.

Substantive check, not merely a bypass artifact: Syndra's only stack-gated inter-slot couplings are the five Transcendent thresholds - Q at 40, W at 60, E at 80, R at 100, P at 120 (all quoted below). At splinters = 120 every threshold is already satisfied unconditionally, so no slot's enhancement is contingent on any other slot's position in the rotation. There is no residual ordering dependency to record.

The remaining kit couplings are positional/CC (W grabs the nearest Dark Sphere; E's stun requires knocking back a Dark Sphere; R 'grabs up to 4 nearby live ones'). data/champion-audit/batch-6.json records E/W CC as utility-only out of scope, and records that 'R reads Magic Damage per Sphere x user-set sphere count' - i.e. the sphere count is a user option (r_spheres), not something resolved from cast ordering. So these also generate zero dependency edges.
Conclusion: six ledgers, each empty, is the correct value - both by the bypass rule and by the independent kit analysis at 120 splinters.

step_4_absence_is_wrong.claim: The old value <absent> cannot be correct.
derivation: An absent leaf cannot distinguish 'the resolver ran and found no dependencies' from 'the resolver was never invoked'. Those are different facts and the second is a silent-failure mode.

This is the same failure class CLAUDE.md rule 5 legislates against elsewhere (a silent fallback silently winning when the upstream breaks). Recording the empty ledgers AND naming the two unconsulted rows is the fail-closed record; omitting the leaf is not.

independent_computation.arithmetic_summary: rows = 5 wiki slots + 1 (Q2, unlocked because 120 >= 40) = 6 ledgers; unconsulted = 2 out-of-scope rows (E/W CC, R execute); edges per ledger = 0 (all Transcendent thresholds 40/60/80/100/120 satisfied at 120; order exogenous via hand seed).

negative_findings: No occurrence of the strings 'dependencies', 'unconsulted', 'resolver', 'custom_order', or 'syndra_custom_order_120' anywhere in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md - the ledger schema itself is not defined by the sourced data, so the shape was reconstructed from the slot/out-of-scope partition in data/champion-audit/batch-6.json rather than read off a schema.

The 6+2 partition therefore rests on the audit's modeled/out_of_scope split; it matches exactly, but a different row-partition convention (e.g. counting auto-attack or item-proc rows) could in principle also yield 6+2. The count is corroborated, not uniquely forced.
confidence: high on the emptiness of the ledgers and on <absent> being wrong; medium-high on the exact 6+2 partition (corroborated by the audit's modeled/out-of-scope split, no schema in data/ to force it).
